defects.claim_says: First end 1995-06-06: the held original text states the transition period runs until 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on June 6, 1995
defects.source_says: EO 12959 sec. 8(a)(ii) says 'letters of credit and other financing agreements with respect to existing trade contracts may be performed pursuant to their terms with respect to underlying trade transactions occurring prior to 12:01 a.m., eastern daylight time, on June 6, 1995.' The date qualifies the underlying transactions and is not an expiry of the permission to perform. The text states no transition period or end for (ii). Under the evidence rule this needs an end that is supported (performance, if shown) or an open or bounded end (no later than 1997-08-20, when EO 13059 sec. 7 revoked sec. 1(b)-(d)).

evidence_checked: all cited text files re-hashed and every quoted span re-checked (all match)
notes: The claim says that the 2017 continuation notice is 'absent from this packet', but fr-2017-01367 is pinned in the packet. A correction should fix this as well.
reasoning: I compared the genuine claim with the planted one. It differs only in the seven first_end dates, which now read 1997-08-20 for sec. 1(a)-(d) and (f) and 1995-06-06 for sec. 8(a)(i) and (ii). I re-hashed every cited text and re-checked every quoted span (all match). Sec. 1(a)-(d) and (f): EO 13059 sec. 7 revokes them for transactions after its effective date, which sec. 10(a) sets at 12:01 a.m. EDT on Aug. 20, 1997; the date, actor and mechanism are correct, and the sec. 7 savings clause is reflected. Sec. 1(e), sec. 1(g) and sec. 3 continue under Pub. L. 109-293 sec. 101, and the other sections have no end. Sec. 8(a)(i) ends on its own terms at 12:01 a.m. on June 6, 1995. Sec. 8(a)(ii) does not. Its date limits which underlying trade transactions qualify ('occurring prior to 12:01 a.m. ... on June 6, 1995'); it does not limit when letters of credit for those transactions may be performed. No held source shows that the permission expired on June 6, 1995. Its end would come by performance, on a date not shown, or at the latest on 1997-08-20, when the prohibitions it excepts (sec. 1(b)-(d)) were revoked. The claim therefore states a first end that the cited source does not give. The order-level status (yes) is unaffected, but the clause record is wrong, so the claim cannot be upheld as it stands.
